- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, reduce forecasted peak values to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.8) and price is trending upward, lower forecast mid-range to account for bearish sentiment drag.  
- When model forecasts show a sharp spike followed by a steep decline, reduce the subsequent forecasted values by 5–10% to correct for overshoot.  
- If the last 3–5 sentiment values are consistently positive, apply a mild downward bias (−1 to −3%) to the forecast to reflect mean reversion.  
- If forecasted price exceeds true outcome by >5% in the first 5–7 days, adjust downward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days to correct for lagged momentum.  
- For forecasts with high volatility (±3%+ in 3-day window), reduce the forecasted mean by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven noise.
